levels.vo_note: ffmpeg ebur128 on spine/ALL.e.enhanced.mp4. mix_music.py raises the voice +2.0 dB by default (GRAPH-PROGRESS settings carry no voice_db), so every seat is computed against the raised voice at -20.4 LUFS.
levels.seat_rule: THREE seats, because the track has a 10 LU range and one seat would bury the verse 26 dB under the voice: rise + chorus rows remotion_gain_db -31.0 (chorus at -39.4 LUFS, 19 dB under the raised voice); verse + build rows -26.0 (-41.3 LUFS, 21 under); breakdown rows -24.0 (-42.2 LUFS, 22 under). The track keeps about 3 LU of its lift into each chorus, and every rise row sits at the chorus seat so a drop is always a real step up. Where a seat changes inside sample-continuous audio the mixer ramps it over 0.5 s at the row boundary (5.865, 92.115, 125.265), always before a drop. No automation rows; no clip inserts in this video (COVER-PLAN clip_inserts is empty).

placement_math.parity: The 2-bar chord loop decides two things. (1) Counted back from the ending the first drop can only fall 7 bars after frame 0 (13.365), so the video opens on bar 9, mid-groove. (2) A chorus can only start on an odd k, so the money drop is 99.615 or 95.865, never 97.7 on Now, and the verdict drop is 125.865 or 122.115, never 123.98 on Therefore. The later line was taken both times: the drum roll gets Now the money, the riser gets Therefore, for most developers.

Everything else is the file playing on, merged by the mixer into one placement per run.
